faq.description: Quick answers to the problems developers most often meet when connecting React to translation resources.

item1.answer: Check the key spelling, letter case, active namespace, JSON syntax, and backend loadPath. i18next returns the key when it cannot resolve a value.
item1.question: Why does the interface show the key instead of the translation?

item2.answer: Enable localStorage in the detector order and caches arrays. The detector can then reuse the user's explicit selection after refresh.
item2.question: Why does the language reset when the page reloads?

item3.answer: Changing the i18next language does not set HTML direction automatically. Update document.documentElement.dir to rtl for Arabic and ltr for English.
item3.question: Why is Arabic still displayed in an LTR layout?

item4.answer: Static analysis cannot predict every runtime value. Prefer literal keys or an explicit key map, then run extraction and status checks again.
item4.question: Why did the CLI miss a dynamic translation key?

faq.title: Common questions, practical answers

practices.description: Small decisions make multilingual projects easier to translate, test, and maintain as they grow.

item1.description: Prefer descriptive paths such as checkout.payment.failed over vague or numbered keys.
item1.title: Name keys by meaning

item2.description: Keep complete sentences together because word order differs between languages.
item2.title: Do not translate fragments

item3.description: Pass names and values through interpolation instead of joining strings manually.
item3.title: Interpolate dynamic data

item4.description: Always pass a numeric count so i18next can choose the correct language form.
item4.title: Respect plural rules

item5.description: Synchronize the document language and direction whenever the active language changes.

item6.description: Run extraction and status checks before releases to catch missing resources early.

setup.description: Follow seven practical stages—from installing the packages and writing resources to switching direction and remembering the user's language.

step1.description: Install the core engine, React bindings, HTTP resource loader, and browser language detector.
step1.point1: i18next manages language rules and resources.
step1.point2: react-i18next connects the engine to components.
step1.point3: Backend and detector handle loading and selection.
step1.title: Install the required packages

step2.description: Create a predictable folder for every locale so the HTTP backend can build resource URLs automatically.
step2.point1: Keep locale files inside the public directory.
step2.point2: Use ISO language codes such as en and ar.
step2.title: Organize your locale files

step3.description: Write matching keys in every language file, then translate values without changing the key structure.
step3.point1: Group related keys into nested objects.
step3.point2: Use interpolation for names and changing values.
step3.point3: Add every plural form required by the language.
step3.title: Create clear translation resources

step4.description: Register the plugins, list supported languages, select a fallback, and point the backend to your JSON files.
step4.point2: Use English when a requested locale is unavailable.
step4.point3: Load JSON resources through a predictable path.
step4.title: Connect the i18next engine

step5.description: Import the configuration once, before React renders any component that calls useTranslation.
step5.point1: Import i18n before importing or rendering App.
step5.point3: Components receive updates through the React binding.
step5.title: Start i18next before React renders

step6.description: Call useTranslation inside a component, render values with t, and switch language with changeLanguage.
step6.point1: Use t with a stable key to render text.
step6.point2: Read resolvedLanguage for the active locale.
step6.title: Use translations inside components

step7.description: Synchronize HTML language and direction, while the detector stores the selected locale for later visits.
step7.point1: Set lang for browsers and assistive technology.
step7.point2: Use rtl for Arabic and ltr for English.
step7.title: Finish with direction and persistence
